response.sql:
WITH scan_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    crewref,
    CASE WHEN gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL AND spanmin != 0 
         THEN gbsize / spanmin 
         ELSE NULL 
    END as gb_per_min
  FROM scans
),
operator_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    crewref,
    COUNT(*) as num_scans,
    AVG(gb_per_min) as avg_gb_per_min
  FROM scan_metrics
  GROUP BY crewref
),
global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(gb_per_min) as global_avg_gb_per_min
  FROM scan_metrics
)
SELECT 
  AVG(os.num_scans) as avg_num_scans,
  AVG(os.avg_gb_per_min) as avg_gb_per_min,
  AVG(os.avg_gb_per_min - ga.global_avg_gb_per_min) as avg_margin
FROM operator_stats os
CROSS JOIN global_avg ga
WHERE os.avg_gb_per_min > ga.global_avg_gb_per_min;

assumptions.assumption: "Ignore missing values" means to exclude scans where gbsize or spanmin are NULL, or where spanmin equals 0, from average GB-per-minute calculations. Division by zero is prevented by checking spanmin != 0.

The global average GB per minute is computed as the mean of gb_per_min across all individual scans (rather than as the mean of each operator's average). This weights operators proportionally to their scan volume.

alternatives.interpretation: The phrase "simple average of that figure across all operators" means the mean of each operator's average GB per minute, treating each operator equally regardless of scan count. This would be computed as AVG(avg_gb_per_min) over operator_stats rather than AVG(gb_per_min) over raw scans.
